# Automata Simulator — Full LLM Reference

> A web-based visual editor and simulator for finite automata (DFA, NFA, PDA) and Turing Machines (TM).
> URL: https://automata.yuweiss.dev
> Source: https://github.com/YuvalWS/automata-simulator
> Summary: https://automata.yuweiss.dev/llms.txt

## JSON Schema (Zod Definitions)

The app validates loaded files using these Zod schemas:

```typescript
const PointSchema = z.object({
  x: z.number(),
  y: z.number(),
});

const ViewportSchema = z.object({
  panX: z.number(),
  panY: z.number(),
  zoom: z.number().positive(),  // must be > 0
});

const AutomatonStateSchema = z.object({
  id: z.string().min(1),
  name: z.string().min(1),
  position: PointSchema,
  isInitial: z.boolean(),
  isAccepting: z.boolean(),
});

const PdaRuleSchema = z.object({
  inputSymbol: z.string(),
  stackPop: z.string(),
  stackPush: z.array(z.string()),
  peekAction: z.enum(['nop', 'push', 'pop']).optional(),
});

// TmRule: readSymbols is a non-empty array (multiple reads collapse into one rule);
// writeSymbol is optional (omit / empty = no-op write — head cell unchanged).
// Files written by v1.3.0 used { readSymbol: string; writeSymbol: string } — the loader
// accepts both shapes and normalizes v1 → v2 at load time.
const TmRuleSchema = z.object({
  readSymbols: z.array(z.string()).min(1),
  writeSymbol: z.string().optional(),
  direction: z.enum(['L', 'R', 'S']),
});

const TransitionSchema = z.object({
  id: z.string().min(1),
  sourceId: z.string().min(1),
  targetId: z.string().min(1),
  symbols: z.array(z.string()),
  pdaRules: z.array(PdaRuleSchema).optional(),
  tmRules: z.array(TmRuleSchema).optional(),
  controlPointOffset: PointSchema.optional(),
});

const AutomatonSchema = z.object({
  id: z.string().min(1),
  name: z.string().min(1),
  type: z.enum(['DFA', 'NFA', 'PDA', 'TM']),
  alphabet: z.array(z.string()),
  states: z.array(AutomatonStateSchema),
  transitions: z.array(TransitionSchema),
  viewport: ViewportSchema,
  acceptanceMode: z.enum(['finalState', 'emptyStack', 'haltOnAccept']).optional(),
  pdaStackMode: z.enum(['pop', 'peek']).optional(),
  tmMode: z.enum(['deterministic', 'nondeterministic']).optional(),
  tmBlankSymbol: z.string().optional(),
});

const SaveFileSchema = z.object({
  version: z.string(),
  automaton: AutomatonSchema,
});
```

## Field Reference

### SaveFile
| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| version | string | File format version, currently `"1.4.0"` |
| automaton | Automaton | The automaton data |

### Automaton
| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| id | string (min 1) | Unique identifier for the automaton |
| name | string (min 1) | Display name shown in the UI |
| type | `"DFA"`, `"NFA"`, `"PDA"`, or `"TM"` | Automaton type |
| alphabet | string[] | List of input symbols (excluding ε; informational for TM) |
| states | State[] | Array of states |
| transitions | Transition[] | Array of transitions |
| viewport | Viewport | Camera position and zoom level |
| acceptanceMode | `"finalState"` / `"emptyStack"` / `"haltOnAccept"` (optional) | PDA: `finalState`/`emptyStack`. TM: `finalState`/`haltOnAccept`. |
| pdaStackMode | `"pop"` / `"peek"` (optional) | PDA only — `pop` consumes the matched stack symbol; `peek` inspects without consuming |
| tmMode | `"deterministic"` / `"nondeterministic"` (optional) | TM only — DTM disallows duplicate rules per `(state, readSymbol)` |
| tmBlankSymbol | string (optional) | TM only — symbol that fills unbounded cells on both sides of the tape (default `"⊔"`) |

### State
| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| id | string (min 1) | Unique identifier |
| name | string (min 1) | Display label (e.g., "q0", "q1") |
| position | {x, y} | Canvas coordinates for visual layout |
| isInitial | boolean | Whether this is the start state (exactly one should be true) |
| isAccepting | boolean | Whether this is an accepting/final state |

### Transition
| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| id | string (min 1) | Unique identifier |
| sourceId | string (min 1) | ID of the source state |
| targetId | string (min 1) | ID of the target state (same as sourceId for self-loops) |
| symbols | string[] | Symbols that trigger this transition (DFA/NFA only) |
| pdaRules | PdaRule[]? | PDA transition rules (mutually exclusive with `symbols`) |
| tmRules | TmRule[]? | TM transition rules (mutually exclusive with `symbols`) |
| controlPointOffset | {x, y}? | Optional offset for curved rendering |

### PdaRule
| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| inputSymbol | string | Input character to consume, or `"ε"` for no input |
| stackPop | string | Symbol that must be on the stack top to apply this rule (or `"ε"` for any) |
| stackPush | string[] | Symbols to push onto the stack (leftmost = new top); empty means no push |
| peekAction | `"nop"` / `"push"` / `"pop"` (optional) | Only relevant when `pdaStackMode === "peek"` |

### TmRule
| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| readSymbols | string[] (min 1) | The rule fires if the head reads any of these symbols. UI label collapses to `0,1,Y → R`. |
| writeSymbol | string (optional) | Symbol to write at the head before moving. Omit (or empty) for a no-op write — the head cell is left unchanged. Textbook shorthand `Y → R`. |
| direction | `"L"` / `"R"` / `"S"` | Move head Left, Right, or Stay |

### Viewport
| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| panX | number | Horizontal pan offset |
| panY | number | Vertical pan offset |
| zoom | number (> 0) | Zoom level (1.0 = 100%) |

## Validation Rules

### DFA-specific rules
- Each state must have at most one transition per input symbol (no nondeterminism)
- Epsilon transitions (`"ε"`, U+03B5) are not allowed
- Ideally, every state has a transition for every symbol in the alphabet (the app warns about missing transitions)

### NFA-specific rules
- Multiple transitions from the same state on the same symbol are allowed
- Epsilon transitions are allowed — use the symbol `"ε"` (U+03B5)
- During simulation, epsilon-closure is computed automatically

### PDA-specific rules
- Transitions use `pdaRules`, not `symbols`. Epsilon-input rules consume no input.
- `stackPop` is matched against the top of the stack (index 0); use `"ε"` to bypass the check.
- The initial stack contains only the bottom marker `"Z₀"` (U+2080).
- `acceptanceMode === "finalState"`: accept if any active configuration is in an accepting state at end of input.
- `acceptanceMode === "emptyStack"`: accept if any configuration has an empty stack at end of input; accepting states are ignored.
- `pdaStackMode === "peek"`: each rule's `peekAction` selects what happens to the stack after the peek.

### TM-specific rules
- Transitions use `tmRules`, not `symbols`. There are no epsilon transitions; the head always reads a tape cell.
- The input word initializes the tape (`[word..., blank, blank, ...]`); head starts at index 0.
- A rule fires when the symbol at the head matches **any** entry in its `readSymbols` array (textbook label `0,1,Y → R`).
- `writeSymbol` is optional. When omitted or empty, the head cell is left unchanged (no-op write, textbook label `Y → R`).
- After applying a rule, the head moves Left, Right, or Stays. The tape grows by one blank cell on either end when the head moves out of bounds.
- `tmMode === "deterministic"`: at most one rule per `(sourceId, readSym)` pair. A multi-read rule expands to one pair per symbol; two rules conflict if they share even one read symbol. Validator emits an error with a "Switch to NTM" action when duplicates are found.
- `tmMode === "nondeterministic"`: branches are explored in parallel (capped at 1000 active configurations).
- `acceptanceMode === "finalState"`: accept on entry to any accepting state (or when a halted branch is in an accepting state).
- `acceptanceMode === "haltOnAccept"`: any branch that halts (no rule matches the current tape cell) is accepted unconditionally; accepting states are ignored.
- Hard step cap: 1000 steps. If the machine has not halted by then, the final snapshot's status is `"timeout"`.
- The `tmBlankSymbol` is a regular tape symbol and is matched literally in rules.

### General rules
- Exactly one state must have `isInitial: true`
- All `sourceId` and `targetId` must reference valid state IDs
- The `alphabet` array should list all symbols used in transitions (ε is excluded from the alphabet)
- IDs must be non-empty strings (UUIDs are commonly used but any non-empty string works)

## Layout Tips

When generating automata for visual display:
- Space states ~200px apart horizontally for readability
- A typical Y coordinate is 200-300 for a single row
- For multi-row layouts, use ~200px vertical spacing
- The viewport `{ panX: 0, panY: 0, zoom: 1 }` is a good default
- State names conventionally use "q0", "q1", "q2", etc.

## Example 1: DFA that accepts strings ending with "ab"

```json
{
  "version": "1.4.0",
  "automaton": {
    "id": "dfa-ends-ab",
    "name": "Ends with ab",
    "type": "DFA",
    "alphabet": ["a", "b"],
    "states": [
      { "id": "s0", "name": "q0", "position": { "x": 100, "y": 200 }, "isInitial": true, "isAccepting": false },
      { "id": "s1", "name": "q1", "position": { "x": 300, "y": 200 }, "isInitial": false, "isAccepting": false },
      { "id": "s2", "name": "q2", "position": { "x": 500, "y": 200 }, "isInitial": false, "isAccepting": true }
    ],
    "transitions": [
      { "id": "t0", "sourceId": "s0", "targetId": "s1", "symbols": ["a"] },
      { "id": "t1", "sourceId": "s0", "targetId": "s0", "symbols": ["b"] },
      { "id": "t2", "sourceId": "s1", "targetId": "s1", "symbols": ["a"] },
      { "id": "t3", "sourceId": "s1", "targetId": "s2", "symbols": ["b"] },
      { "id": "t4", "sourceId": "s2", "targetId": "s1", "symbols": ["a"] },
      { "id": "t5", "sourceId": "s2", "targetId": "s0", "symbols": ["b"] }
    ],
    "viewport": { "panX": 0, "panY": 0, "zoom": 1 }
  }
}
```

## Example 2: NFA with epsilon transitions (accepts "a*b*")

```json
{
  "version": "1.4.0",
  "automaton": {
    "id": "nfa-a-star-b-star",
    "name": "a*b* (NFA with ε)",
    "type": "NFA",
    "alphabet": ["a", "b"],
    "states": [
      { "id": "s0", "name": "q0", "position": { "x": 100, "y": 200 }, "isInitial": true, "isAccepting": false },
      { "id": "s1", "name": "q1", "position": { "x": 300, "y": 200 }, "isInitial": false, "isAccepting": true }
    ],
    "transitions": [
      { "id": "t0", "sourceId": "s0", "targetId": "s0", "symbols": ["a"] },
      { "id": "t1", "sourceId": "s0", "targetId": "s1", "symbols": ["ε"] },
      { "id": "t2", "sourceId": "s1", "targetId": "s1", "symbols": ["b"] }
    ],
    "viewport": { "panX": 0, "panY": 0, "zoom": 1 }
  }
}
```

## Example 3: DFA with self-loop (accepts even number of a's)

```json
{
  "version": "1.4.0",
  "automaton": {
    "id": "dfa-even-a",
    "name": "Even number of a's",
    "type": "DFA",
    "alphabet": ["a", "b"],
    "states": [
      { "id": "s0", "name": "even", "position": { "x": 100, "y": 200 }, "isInitial": true, "isAccepting": true },
      { "id": "s1", "name": "odd", "position": { "x": 350, "y": 200 }, "isInitial": false, "isAccepting": false }
    ],
    "transitions": [
      { "id": "t0", "sourceId": "s0", "targetId": "s1", "symbols": ["a"] },
      { "id": "t1", "sourceId": "s0", "targetId": "s0", "symbols": ["b"] },
      { "id": "t2", "sourceId": "s1", "targetId": "s0", "symbols": ["a"] },
      { "id": "t3", "sourceId": "s1", "targetId": "s1", "symbols": ["b"] }
    ],
    "viewport": { "panX": 0, "panY": 0, "zoom": 1 }
  }
}
```

## Example 4: PDA for a^n b^n (final-state acceptance)

```json
{
  "version": "1.4.0",
  "automaton": {
    "id": "pda-anbn",
    "name": "a^n b^n",
    "type": "PDA",
    "alphabet": ["a", "b"],
    "states": [
      { "id": "s0", "name": "q0", "position": { "x": 100, "y": 200 }, "isInitial": true,  "isAccepting": false },
      { "id": "s1", "name": "q1", "position": { "x": 300, "y": 200 }, "isInitial": false, "isAccepting": false },
      { "id": "s2", "name": "qf", "position": { "x": 500, "y": 200 }, "isInitial": false, "isAccepting": true }
    ],
    "transitions": [
      { "id": "t0", "sourceId": "s0", "targetId": "s0", "symbols": [],
        "pdaRules": [{ "inputSymbol": "a", "stackPop": "Z₀", "stackPush": ["A", "Z₀"] }] },
      { "id": "t1", "sourceId": "s0", "targetId": "s0", "symbols": [],
        "pdaRules": [{ "inputSymbol": "a", "stackPop": "A", "stackPush": ["A", "A"] }] },
      { "id": "t2", "sourceId": "s0", "targetId": "s1", "symbols": [],
        "pdaRules": [{ "inputSymbol": "ε", "stackPop": "A", "stackPush": ["A"] }] },
      { "id": "t3", "sourceId": "s1", "targetId": "s1", "symbols": [],
        "pdaRules": [{ "inputSymbol": "b", "stackPop": "A", "stackPush": [] }] },
      { "id": "t4", "sourceId": "s1", "targetId": "s2", "symbols": [],
        "pdaRules": [{ "inputSymbol": "ε", "stackPop": "Z₀", "stackPush": ["Z₀"] }] }
    ],
    "viewport": { "panX": 0, "panY": 0, "zoom": 1 },
    "acceptanceMode": "finalState",
    "pdaStackMode": "pop"
  }
}
```

## Example 5: Turing Machine that flips a single `0` to `1`

```json
{
  "version": "1.4.0",
  "automaton": {
    "id": "tm-flip",
    "name": "Flip 0 to 1",
    "type": "TM",
    "alphabet": ["0", "1"],
    "states": [
      { "id": "s0", "name": "q0", "position": { "x": 100, "y": 200 }, "isInitial": true,  "isAccepting": false },
      { "id": "s1", "name": "q1", "position": { "x": 300, "y": 200 }, "isInitial": false, "isAccepting": false },
      { "id": "s2", "name": "qf", "position": { "x": 500, "y": 200 }, "isInitial": false, "isAccepting": true }
    ],
    "transitions": [
      { "id": "t0", "sourceId": "s0", "targetId": "s1", "symbols": [],
        "tmRules": [{ "readSymbols": ["0"], "writeSymbol": "1", "direction": "R" }] },
      { "id": "t1", "sourceId": "s1", "targetId": "s2", "symbols": [],
        "tmRules": [{ "readSymbols": ["⊔"], "direction": "S" }] }
    ],
    "viewport": { "panX": 0, "panY": 0, "zoom": 1 },
    "tmMode": "deterministic",
    "tmBlankSymbol": "⊔",
    "acceptanceMode": "finalState"
  }
}
```

## How to Use Generated JSON

### Desktop
1. Save the JSON to a `.json` file
2. Open https://automata.yuweiss.dev
3. Click "Load" (or press Ctrl+O) and select the file
4. The automaton will render with all states, transitions, and layout preserved

### Mobile / Tablet
1. Save the JSON to a `.json` file
2. Open https://automata.yuweiss.dev on your phone or tablet
3. Tap the hamburger menu (top-left) and tap "Load"
4. Select the JSON file from your device
5. The automaton will render with full touch interaction support (tap, drag, pinch-zoom, long-press)

## Describing Automata in Natural Language

When asked to explain an automaton JSON file:
1. Identify the type (DFA/NFA/PDA/TM) and the alphabet
2. Identify the initial state and accepting state(s); for TM also note `tmBlankSymbol`, `tmMode`, and `acceptanceMode`
3. Describe the transition function (DFA/NFA: symbols; PDA: input/pop/push triples; TM: read/write/move triples)
4. Describe the language the automaton accepts in set-builder notation or plain English
5. Note any self-loops and their purpose
